summary.one_line: Small US residential contractors do price jobs in spreadsheets and lose money on markup, overhead and labour-hour mistakes, but basic estimate templates are given away free by software vendors and dozens of AI-built sites, so Bidline only earns money if its paid kit sells the profit loop (overhead recovery, labour hours, estimate vs actual) rather than a template.

go_hold.subject: Bidline paid Estimating Kit
go_hold.rationale: Real, large audience and verified spreadsheet behaviour, plus paid bundles at $9-$109 on Etsy and Gumroad. But the free-template market is saturated and earlier FORGE research ranked a trades estimate pack last. Proceed only with a differentiated kit; keep investment small until first-party sales prove demand.
go_hold.falsifying_test: If the kit is live, checkout works and Bidline gets at least 300 organic sessions to the kit page within 60 days of launch with zero sales, move Bidline to hold and shift Stage 2 to Quilt Plan Kit. Thresholds are owner-adjustable decision rules, not forecasts.

key_findings.statement: There were 2,875,590 nonemployer construction businesses in the US in 2022, with $238.0B in receipts (9.6% of all nonemployer establishments).
Small contractors describe estimating in Excel or Google Sheets: unit-cost sheets, labour hours by phase, and comparing estimates with actual job cost.
key_findings.notes: One thread, about 12 replies; qualitative only.

key_findings.statement: Basic estimate templates are offered free by field-service software vendors (e.g. Housecall Pro) and many template sites, so a basic template has little standalone value.
Paid contractor template bundles exist at $3.99 single sheets, $9 three-packs, $19 eight-tool packs, and $109 for a 17-pack; trade-specific packs sell around $45.
The $109 17-template Etsy bundle shows 9 shop sales in 5 months and no reviews, a weak demand signal for high-priced template bundles.
Search results for contractor pricing topics include several small AI-built template sites on free hosting, so competition for these keywords is rising.
Search volume for contractor estimating keywords is unknown.

premium_product_recommendation.name: Bidline Estimating Kit
premium_product_recommendation.format: Excel workbook (also opens in Google Sheets) + one-page quick-start PDF + filled example job
must_include: Overhead recovery: a year of overhead / yearly billable hours = true hourly cost
Labour hours by phase x rate, separate from materials
Reusable unit-cost price book the estimate pulls from
Correct pricing by target margin, with markup shown alongside
Estimate vs actual job-cost tab that flags misses and feeds the price book
A complete worked example the buyer can copy and adapt
must_not: Be the free template renamed (the current paid file is byte-identical to the free one, per WS3)
Claim it guarantees profit or wins bids
Require macros (blocked in Google Sheets and many Excel setups)
premium_product_recommendation.why_they_pay: Free templates format a quote; contractors pay to stop losing money. The paid kit answers 'what should I charge so this job actually makes money', which forum users currently build by hand.

offer_ladder.item: Estimate calculator, markup/margin converter, basic template
Trade edition or kit + trade price-book bundle

premium_product_recommendation.falsifying_test: Zero sales from the first 300 organic sessions on the kit page within 60 days of checkout going live means the offer or audience is wrong; hold and re-research.

$19 matches the main competitor bundle price; a $29 test is justified once the job-costing loop exists.
evidence.notes: Launch at the approved $19 (Lemon Squeezy test product is $19.99; align it). Any price change needs owner approval.

unit_economics.statement: Lemon Squeezy takes about 5% + $0.50 per order, so a $19 sale nets about $17.55 before tax.

At about $17.55 net per $19 sale, $100 a month needs 6 sales and $400 a month needs 23. The kill rule in this brief (300+ kit-page sessions in 60 days with no sale) stays the test of whether any of this demand exists. This is arithmetic on the estimated fee, not a forecast.
